svg.title: Requests, checks, decisions and later withdrawal
svg.desc: Example: a museum-entry encounter. The access seeker (example: visitor) and the resource controller (example: museum) make contact and state what they want. The resource controller requests the age-threshold answer, permission to keep that answer for up to twenty-four hours, separate permission to keep an access record and permission for marketing contact. The access seeker requests controller evidence and access conditions. Each authenticates the other Entity and its request before sharing information beyond the authentication minimum. The access seeker permits the age-threshold answer for the access decision and its retention for up to twenty-four hours, separately permits a minimal access record for up to twenty-four hours, and denies marketing contact. The resource controller permits its controller evidence. The access seeker checks that evidence and the access conditions. If it accepts them, the access seeker sends the age-threshold answer. The resource controller checks the answer as Verifier and grants access if the evidence is sufficient. Each keeps its own minimal Receipt. Either Entity can later withdraw a Grant it gave. The example shows the resource controller withdrawing access at its controlled source and rejecting further access even when notice was missed. Arrows show what depends on what, not required network messages.
svg.text: Checks come before sharing beyond the authentication minimum
1. Make contact: each states what it is and what it wants
Each decides whether it needs anything from the other.

g.text: 2. Request age-threshold answer and separate permissions
Declare purpose, data use and how long records will be kept
3. Request controller evidence and access conditions
Declare intended use and retention
4. Each authenticates the other Entity and its request
Only the authentication minimum is shared at this stage.
5. Age-threshold answer: use, keep up to 24 hours
Access record: permitted for up to 24 hours.
Access seeker denies marketing contact.
5. Controller evidence: permitted
Access waits for the age-threshold check.
6. Resource controller's authorized controller evidence
Access seeker checks the evidence and access conditions.
7. If accepted, access seeker sends the age-threshold answer
Resource controller checks that item as Verifier.
8. Resource controller grants access if evidence is sufficient
Access seeker uses it only if evidence and conditions are acceptable.
9. Each keeps a minimal, trustworthy Receipt
Only actual checks and decisions; sharing needs permission.
Failed checks or unmet conditions: withhold information or decline
Continue only if the remaining conditions and permissions allow it.
Later withdrawal
Either Entity can withdraw a Grant it gave.
Shown: the resource controller withdraws access at its controlled source.
Access seeker requests access again
Access rejected despite old Grant or missed notice
The stages show what depends on what, not a required message sequence.
